newsitem.title: USA: Lake told Clinton in letter he lost patience.
newsitem.headline: Lake told Clinton in letter he lost patience.

text.p: Anthony Lake told President Clinton in a letter he withdrew his nomination to be director of the CIA because he had lost patience with a confirmation process that had become a "political circus," published reports said Tuesday.

The New York Times and Washington Post published the letter in which Lake said: "After more than three months, I have finally lost patience and the endless delays are hurting the CIA and the NSC (National Security Council) staff in ways I am no longer able to tolerate."

Lake, Clinton's first-term national security adviser, urged the President to withdraw his nomination in a White House meeting Monday, an administration source said. He followed up the meeting with a letter explaining the reasons, the source said.

The decision followed three days of tough confimation hearings last week in which members of the Senate Intelligence Committee questioned Lake's integrity, management skills and fitness to head the agency.
"It now seems certain the committee deliberations will extend past the recess until after Easter, and probably longer," Lake said in the letter.
Lake said the confirmation process, "mired in partisan politics," was having a damaging effect on the Central Intelligence Agency and its staff deserved better.

"I have gone through the past three months and more with patience and I hope, dignity," he said. "But I have lost the former and could lose the latter as this political circus continues indefinitely."
